newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate inches up 10 bps to 11.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate inches up 10 bps to 11.2 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate inched up ten basis points to 11.2 percent in balanced trade on Tuesday, only half of which was fresh borrowing.
The day's trade was modest at 40.4 million kuna but demand for 2.6 million found no lenders.
Short six- to ten-day deals made up most of the fresh transactions, their weighted rate slightly lower at 10.2 percent. Call-money stood at ten percent.
Insurers rolled over the old one-week borrowings at a steady nine percent rate and issued a single one-day loan at 14 percent.
Bankers charged slightly more for one-week loans at rates varying between 10.5 and 11.5 percent.
The Central bank's kuna midrates firmed slightly to 6.1888 against the dollar and to 3.5662 versus the German mark. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
